newsitem.title: USA: pcOrder hires former Compaq exec as CEO.
newsitem.headline: pcOrder hires former Compaq exec as CEO.

text.p: pcOrder.com, a privately held company which sells personal computers over the Internet, said that it hired Ross Cooley, a long-time senior executive at Compaq Computer Corp, as its chairman and chief executive.
Cooley, with Compaq since 1984, was senior vice president and general manager, North America, at Compaq. He was responsible for Compaq's $7 billion U.S. and Canadian computer business.
"My feelings in joining pcOrder are similar to those I had in joining Compaq almost 13 years ago," Cooley said.
Before joining Compaq in 1984, Cooley held several sales and marketing positions at International Business Machines Corp, where he worked for 18 years.
Cooley's retirement from Compaq had been rumored for several months. pcOrder.com said that Cooley will be paid $1 a year, plus stock options. pcOrder for now is still private.
pcOrder founder Christina Jones continues as company president. The post of chairman and CEO had been vacant since the start-up was founded in June.
Separately, Compaq replaced Cooley with James Schraith of Cerplex Group Inc, as part of a major sales revamp.

In a major reorganization of its sales structure, Compaq created a new position of senior vice president, general manager, worldwide sales and appointed Richard Synder, formerly an executive with Dell Computer Corp.
All the five geographies, Asia Pacific, Europe, Middle East and Africa, Japan, Latin America and North America, will now report directly to Synder, as well as worldwide customer support functions.
Previously, the heads of these regions reported directly to Compaq CEO Eckhard Pfeiffer.
